# Paweł Ostromecki

> Senior software engineer and consultant from Wrocław, Poland, working remotely worldwide. He builds software for companies: web and mobile apps, websites and AI workflows, plus audits and maintenance. He focuses on fintech, regtech and e-commerce, and leads the Angular Wrocław community.

## Services

- [AI workflows](https://www.ostromecki.dev/services): take a manual, repetitive process such as ordering, ticket triage, document checks or data entry, design an LLM or agent workflow around it, and plug it into the tools a team already uses.
- [AI in real business cases](https://www.ostromecki.dev/services): take a real process from a business and improve it with AI, from the first prototype to a working solution in production.
- [Web applications](https://www.ostromecki.dev/services): client portals, admin panels, booking and order systems, and internal tools that replace spreadsheets.
- [Mobile apps](https://www.ostromecki.dev/services): iOS and Android apps, as part of a larger system or standalone, shipped to the App Store and Google Play.
- [Websites](https://www.ostromecki.dev/services): company websites and landing pages, fast, and visible in search engines and to AI alike.
- [Application audit](https://www.ostromecki.dev/services): an independent review of code, architecture, security and performance, with fixes ranked by impact.
- [Maintenance and development](https://www.ostromecki.dev/services): fixes, updates, monitoring and new features across the system's whole lifecycle.

Ways to start with AI: Discovery (1 to 2 weeks), Pilot (4 to 8 weeks). The first 30-minute consultation is free and without commitment.

## Prices

Starting points, net of VAT. The final price depends on scope and is given in a written quote after a free 30-minute call.

- Websites: from $500 (Polish clients: from 1,900 PLN)
- Web and mobile apps: from $2,500 (Polish clients: from 9,000 PLN)
- Maintenance and development: from $29 a month (Polish clients: from 99 PLN a month)
- AI workflows, AI projects and audits: quoted individually

## How it works

- A free 30-minute call, without commitment; he replies within 1 business day.
- A written quote with scope, price and timeline.
- Work in stages the client can see and judge along the way.
- A deposit to start and the rest after the client accepts the work; a VAT invoice.
- Code, documentation and designs belong to the client.

## Who it is for

Companies that want to automate a real process with AI, or need an app, website, audit or maintenance. His industry focus is fintech, regtech and e-commerce. He is based in Wrocław, Poland, and works remotely with teams worldwide; on-site workshops are possible.

## Technologies

Google Cloud, Firebase, Python, TypeScript, Angular, React and NestJS. AI features are built on the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications.

## Use cases

- [Agentic replenishment for a salon network](https://www.ostromecki.dev/use-cases/salon-replenishment): salons order stock from HQ in plain language, and an AI agent turns the request into a checked proposal.
- [No-code forms for a regulated industry](https://www.ostromecki.dev/use-cases/no-code-forms): a client-owned drag-and-drop platform for compliance forms, worked on as an external contractor.

## Community

He leads Angular Wrocław, a community of regular meetups for local Angular and frontend developers, with talks, workshops and mentoring. He speaks at meetups and conferences and runs workshops on AI workflows for engineering and business teams.

## Blog posts

- [Code Became Cheap. Did Developer Knowledge Become Cheap Too?](https://www.ostromecki.dev/blog/code-became-cheap): AI made much of what a developer learns cheap, but cheaper code is not a cheaper good decision.
- [Mastering Angular's Host Property](https://www.ostromecki.dev/blog/mastering-angular-host-property): how the host property replaces @HostListener and @HostBinding, works with signals, and how to migrate.
- [You (don't) need another state management library](https://www.ostromecki.dev/blog/you-dont-need-another-state-management-library): signals and a few RxJS operators give the Redux benefits without another dependency.
- [You (don't) need another state management library, vol. 2](https://www.ostromecki.dev/blog/you-dont-need-another-state-management-library2): the same Flux-like pattern with connect from ngxtension, without manual subscriptions.
